set.approach: The ice arena sits on the north side of Route 25A, a few miles west of Wentworth, just above Lower Baker Pond. Park in the plowed pull-out on the south side of the road, across from the pond. The climbs are a very short walk from the road, on the cliff above the pond.

review.notes: Area page gave the road, the pull-out and the short walk. No source says how routes here are descended, so no descent written.

set.approach: Hike the Cascade Brook Trail to its junction, then take the spur trail that heads southwest toward the summit. Where the spur ends short of the top, drop down a snow gully into the ravine to reach the base of the ice. The ravine is an avalanche-prone amphitheater, so check the avalanche forecast and avoid going up when a big storm is arriving.

review.notes: Area page gave the trail sequence and the descent into the ravine. Single source, area-level directions. No source gives the route's own descent.

set.approach: Start at the Lafayette Place trailhead and follow the Old Bridle Path to a sharp left turn, then leave the path and descend among the trees to a former logging road that runs beside the brook. Continue up the brook past two side gullies. The left-hand gully leads to a different route, so stay in the main drainage. It steepens to an iced dihedral known as the Throat, and steep snow leads to the base of the ice.
set.descent_text: Above the ice, several short bulges lead into krummholz, which you work through angling right to reach the ridge. From the ridge you can go left toward Lafayette and descend the Old Bridle Path, or go right over Lincoln and descend the Falling Waters Trail. Check the avalanche forecast, as the gully collects snow.

review.notes: Route page gave the approach, the top-out at the ridge and both walk-offs. The area page confirms the Lafayette Place trailhead (Falling Waters / Old Bridle Path). Single detailed source, so medium.

set.approach: Cross Route 25 from the pull-off at Oliverian Notch and head uphill to the south toward the Appalachian Trail. After a bit over a mile you reach a bog, which is best crossed on snowshoes. From the bog's southeast corner, climb to a small ravine holding several flows. The ravine is the amphitheater itself.

review.notes: Area page gave the route from the road to the ravine. The wording of the distance was garbled in the source so none is given. No descent source.

set.approach: Park near the base of the ski trails, away from the no-parking signs. Walk up the southernmost (leftmost) ski trail for a short way, then head south into the woods. Use the talus and scree below the broken crags as a guide up the steeper hillside. The ice forms in the gully between two broken crags, to the left of the main crag.

review.notes: Area page gave the approach in general terms. Single source; no route-specific description, so no descent written.

set.approach: Follow the stream known as the Cave Route until a fire line trail crosses it, then go up right of the stream through woods and snow-covered slabs to a plateau. Drop down the plateau's northwest side toward the stream and traverse right into open woods. Follow the streambed until it becomes a gully, then stay on the ridge east of the gully to the top where the crags are. Traverse below the cliff line to the middle tree line under the ledges, which avoids the boulder-filled ravine below the ice.

review.notes: Area page gave the approach to the central cliff line, where the one ice route is. Single source. The only descent mentioned is for the rock climbs, not tied to this route, so no descent written.

set.approach: Follow the Greeley Ponds Trail in toward the ponds from the Kancamagus Highway. Before reaching the water, look up to the southwest through the trees to pick out the ridge that holds the ice. The flows are reached by leaving the trail and climbing toward that ridge, so check the avalanche forecast before going.

review.notes: Area page gave the trail, the direction to look for the ridge, and the winter-dependence of the ice. Single source, area-level; no route-specific approach or descent text, so no descent written.
